utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-97-25/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Sava Todovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Todovic. His microphone, please. Mr. Todovic, I want to make sure that you are receiving interpretation in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good afternoon to you. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. My name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff. I appear today with trial attorney Christina Moeller, and case manager, Sebastian van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good afternoon to you and your team. Appearances for the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Aleksandar Lazarevic, counsel for the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, and good afternoon to you too. We had the Initial Appearance a few weeks ago, on the 19th of January - correct me if I'm wrong - and that Initial Appearance could not be concluded in a complete manner because, pursuant to a right that the accused has in terms of our Rules, he chose to postpone entering his plea to the charges brought against him in this indictment within the term of 30 days that are allowed to him, a right which, of course, this Trial Chamber needed to respect. The 30 days are coming to an end, so it is my responsibility now, as the Pre-Trial Judge in charge of the Initial Appearance, to inquire whether your client, Mr. Lazarevic, wishes to enter a plea today, in which case we will proceed according to the Rules. If he doesn't wish to enter a plea, there is a provision that I am sure you are aware of and your client is also, I assume, aware of that I will enter a plea on his behalf, of not guilty. So have you discussed with your client what the position is?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. And I am pleased to inform the Court on his behalf that, according to Rule 62, paragraph 4, he will not enter a plea today again, so he decided not to plead today, and the Trial Chamber will consequently decide that he pleaded not guilty on his behalf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but is that -- can I have a calendar, please? Can I have -- do you have a calendar available? I need to count the dates from the 19th of January until today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I don't have it with me, but I believe that the Registry has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because I know that the 30 days are at an end, but I want to make sure whether they will lapse today or whether there is still time. I think we're talking of 28 today.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Twenty-nine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Twenty-nine today, 29 today. So there is an extra, an additional day, which he can -- he is entitled to make use of. I cannot ask him, I cannot force him to tell me whether his decision basically means that even tomorrow he will not enter a plea. But I think that the right way to go about it is that I can only enter a plea on his behalf after the 30 days have lapsed and he has not entered a plea or if he confirms to me today that, although there is a day or two left, he will not be entering a plea in the remaining time period, in which case, then I will enter a plea on his behalf. I think I will not ask him directly. I'm asking you and you ask him, and then you can tell me, and then I will ask him to confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will have a very brief discussion with him in a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I have had a discussion with the client and he is ready to confirm that he will not enter a plea in any way, I mean tomorrow or the day after tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Todovic, do you confirm what your counsel, Mr. Lazarevic, has just stated? In other words, that it is not your intention to enter a plea, neither today, nor tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can confirm what Mr. Lazarevic said, meaning that I have no intention of pleading over the following two days. I will use this opportunity that the Rules provide for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you, Mr. Todovic. You may sit down. In view of this, the Pre-Trial Judge, having seen Rule 62(A)(iv), namely, that if the -- "If the accused fails to enter a plea at the Initial or any Further Appearance, the Trial Chamber or the Judge shall enter a plea of not guilty on the accused's behalf." And since the accused has stated open -- in open session today that it is not his intention to enter a plea, neither today, nor tomorrow, which will be the -- when the 30 days will expire, the Judge in charge of the -- as Judge in charge of the Initial Appearance, I am hereby entering a plea of not guilty to each and every one of the 18 counts that are brought against the accused by the relative indictment. I will go through the counts one by one for formality. In the first count, the accused is being charged with persecution on political, racial, and/or religious grounds, this being a crime against humanity. I am entering a plea of not guilty for -- on behalf of the accused in relation to this first count. In relation to the second count, which is a charge of torture as a crime against humanity, I am also entering a plea of not guilty on behalf of the accused. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. The third count is one of torture, being a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949. As the Judge in charge of the Initial Appearance, and in terms of the Rule mentioned earlier, I am entering a plea of not guilty on behalf of the accused in relation to this third count. I am also entering a plea of not guilty on behalf of the accused in relation to the fourth count, which is a charge of torture as a violation of the laws or customs of war. In relation to the fifth count, which is one of inhumane acts as a crime against humanity, I, as the Judge in charge of the pre-trial -- of the Initial Appearance, I am entering a plea of not guilty on behalf of the accused. The same applies to the sixth count, to which I am entering a plea of not guilty on behalf of the accused, this count being one consisting of a charge of wilfully causing serious injury to body or health, this being a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949. I am also entering a plea of not guilty to the seventh count on behalf of the accused, this being a charge of cruel treatment as a violation of the laws or customs of war. As regards the eighth count, I am also entering a plea of not guilty on behalf of the accused, this being a charge of murder, being a crime against humanity. I am also entering a plea of not guilty to the ninth count, on behalf of the accused, this being a charge of wilful killing as a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949. The same applies to Count 10. I am entering a plea of not guilty to Count 10, this being a charge of murder as a violation of the laws or customs of war. As regards the eleventh count, which contains a charge of imprisonment as a crime against humanity, I, as the Judge in charge of the Initial Appearance, am entering a plea of not guilty on behalf of the accused. The same applies to the twelfth count, which consists of a charge of unlawful confinement of a civilian as a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949. On behalf of the accused, and in terms of the sub-Rule mentioned earlier, I enter a plea of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, would you please read a bit slower. I thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I apologise to the interpreters for going so fast. The same applies to the thirteenth count, which comprises a charge of inhumane acts, these being a crime against humanity. As the Judge in charge of the Initial Appearance, and as charged by the sub-Rule mentioned earlier, I am entering a plea of not guilty to this count on behalf of the accused. We come to the fourteenth count. To this count, I am entering also a plea of not guilty on behalf of the accused. This count consists of a charge of wilfully causing great suffering, this being a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949. I am further entering a plea of not guilty to the fifteenth count of the indictment, which is a charge of cruel treatment as a violation of the laws or customs of war. I am entering this plea on behalf of the accused and pursuant to what I am charged with doing by the sub-Rule mentioned earlier. I am also entering a plea of not guilty to the sixteenth count, which is a charge of enslavement, this being a crime against humanity. Again, I am entering this plea of not guilty on behalf of the accused as empowered and directed by the said sub-Rule. As regards the seventeenth count, which is a charge of inhumane treatment, this being a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, I am, on behalf of the accused, entering a plea of not guilty. And finally, as regard the eighteenth count, which is a charge of slavery, this being a violation of the laws or customs of war, I am entering a plea of not guilty on behalf of the accused as empowered by the sub-Rule mentioned by me earlier on. Before I adjourn, I would like to ask the Prosecution if there is any matter that they would like to raise.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And the accused himself, now that you have been here for almost a month, or a month, do you -- would you like to address me on any complaint that you might have in relation to your status at the Detention Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours, I have no complaints. I have been treated fairly, and I have no further objections or remarks to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. You may sit down. I bring to an end this continued Initial Appearance, and of course I will, in the coming weeks, appoint a Pre-Trial Judge to be seized with the pre-trial proceedings. You will, of course, be informed in due course, Mr. Lazarevic. And there will be a Status Conference which will be convened within the 120 days from January the 19th, which was the date of the Initial Appearance, okay? Thank you, and good afternoon to everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: adjourned at 1.20 p.m.
